statement: A graph in which the neighbourhood of every vertex induces a Hamiltonian subgraph (a locally Hamiltonian graph) is itself Hamiltonian; equivalently, every maximal planar graph is Hamiltonian.
definitions: The claim under test is: every locally Hamiltonian graph is Hamiltonian, where 'locally Hamiltonian' means the subgraph induced by the open neighbourhood of each vertex has a Hamiltonian cycle (so every vertex has degree at least 3); the clause about maximal planar graphs is a special case (every triangulation on at least 4 vertices is locally Hamiltonian), not an asserted equivalence to be refuted. A graph is Hamiltonian if it has a cycle through all its vertices (at least 3 vertices). A counterexample is an explicit locally Hamiltonian graph (equivalently, an explicit maximal planar graph) together with a verification that it has no Hamiltonian cycle.
